subject: Dedicated capacity: segregated pool priorities, scaling intent & SLA targets
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: emily.park@lumabio.com, adam.jansen@lumabio.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-26T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: segregated pool priorities, scaling intent & SLA targets

Hi Emily / Adam —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same action map. I captured the key pain points, what success looks like, and the next asks so procurement/infra can move forward: 

Pain points we heard
- Production latency spikes for bursty model scoring (video-derived features) during end-of-month runs — 95th pct latency > 4s.
- Need strict tenant isolation for PHI-derived workloads (audit + KMS separation).
- Current self-hosted cluster runs out of preemptible capacity frequently; they want guaranteed throughput for prediction windows.

Goals / acceptance criteria you mentioned
- Dedicated pool for LumaBio models (isolate PHI workloads) with predictable throughput for 50k inference ops/day and burst headroom to ~200k/day.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability for serving endpoints, P95 latency < 200ms for text/metadata requests (video post-processing longer tail tolerable but must stay within cost envelope).
- Data controls: per-customer KMS key option + 12-month retention by default, longer retention as a contract add-on.

Proposed Redwood approach (summary)
- Dedicated reserved GPU pool (tenant-segregated) with optional burst queueing to our shared pool for off-peak elasticity.
- Isolation model: network segmentation + customer-specific key ring + audit logging shipped to their log collector.
- Initial sizing recommendation: 8x A100-equivalent slots for baseline throughput, with two surge slots and autoscale policy tuned to your monthly 95%-ile patterns. Will validate after we get traffic snapshot.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Emily/Adam: share a 7-day traffic snapshot (hourly token counts / batch size distribution) and any security questionnaire items (ops+procurement@lumabio.com) — ETA: EOD Thursday 7/29.
2) Redwood (Ben + Jordan): produce a short MAAP estimate (cost/year) and a segregation risk matrix describing exactly which controls meet PHI isolation — ETA: Tue 8/2. (Attaching initial template).
3) Rishi / Monica: prepare an ops runbook highlight for deploying model updates to the dedicated pool (will be part of the SOW).

Attachments: LumaBio_MAAP_estimates.xlsx (placeholder template), segregation-risks-matrix.pdf (controls template)

If this looks right I’ll share a one-page commercial stub and a proposed pilot timeline. Anything I mis-captured?

Thanks —
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: LumaBio_MAAP_estimates.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB), segregation-risks-matrix.pdf (pdf, 45KB)

From: Emily Park <emily.park@lumabio.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Adam Jansen <adam.jansen@lumabio.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: segregated pool priorities, scaling intent & SLA targets

Ben —

This is a great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 50k/day baseline is accurate for current production; however, our modeling shows a predictable monthly spike (~3x) during model retrain and batch scoring windows. We need the pilot to demonstrate graceful degradation before leaning on autoscale.
- For PHI isolation, we need the KMS separation to be customer-keyed (we manage keys) and remote attestation that the private pool has no routing to other tenants. Network ACLs + HSM-based key wrapping is preferable.
- SLA: 99.9% availability is acceptable as a starting commercial ask; for P95 latency we actually want the 200ms floor for small text calls. Video inference (post-processing) can be up to 1s, as long as we have visibility into queuing.

I've uploaded a short traffic dump and a CSV of recent requests (hourly token count + average batch size) to our ops mailbox — see attachment (traffic-snapshot-202607.csv). Procurement will follow with any contract redlines next week.

We are OK to proceed with the pilot if the MAAP estimate stays within the ballpark of our internal expectation (we budgeted ~$200k/yr for the initial dedicated slice).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Emily
VP, Infrastructure — LumaBio

---
Attachment stubs: traffic-snapshot-202607.csv (csv, 120KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@lumabio.com>, Adam Jansen <adam.jansen@lumabio.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-26T13:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: segregated pool priorities, scaling intent & SLA targets

Emily — great, thanks for the data. I pulled the CSV and forwarded to Jordan for sizing. Three quick notes / confirmations:

1) Pilot proposal
- 8 reserved A100-equivalents (baseline), 2 hot-surge slots, 1-week pilot window to validate P95 latency and isolation.
- Pilot SLOs: 99.5% availability for pilot (commercial SLA to 99.9% for contracted year), P95 latency target 200ms for text calls, video allowed up to 1s.

2) Isolation controls we will include in the pilot
- Customer-controlled KMS integration (we'll provide the integration runbook; you keep keys).
- Network segmentation + explicit routing policy (no egress to shared tenant networks).
- Audit stream delivered to your Splunk/Logstore endpoint (retention configurable).

3) Cost signal and MAAP
- Initial MAAP estimate attached (LumaBio_MAAP_estimates.xlsx) — high level only. Jordan will follow with a slightly tighter number after he ingests the CSV. If we are north of $200k/yr we will call it out explicitly and provide optimization levers (batching, quantization profile, reduced tail latency options).

Next steps: Jordan will circulate a sizing snapshot and a pilot timeline by EOD. Once procurement signals intent we’ll draft a pilot SOW and a short commercial term sheet.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: segregated pool priorities, scaling intent & SLA targets

Quick ops alignment — I ingested the CSV and ran a first-pass sizing. Key operational notes for the pilot: 

- Baseline 8-slot config looks right for steady state; peak-day headroom triggers at 6-hour windows where burst > 2.5x. I recommend we enable a conservative queueing policy during the pilot rather than immediate burst to shared pool (we can show charts for both).
- Runbook additions: (1) rolling model swap procedure, (2) emergency rollback path to a cached model variant if queueing exceeds 30s, (3) warmup policy for new model weights to avoid cold-KV cache misses. Will draft these and attach to the pilot SOW.
- Infra ask for LumaBio: provide us read-only access to a retention copy of the audit logs for the pilot (we will not store PHI beyond the session).

I'll post the sizing spreadsheet to the shared Drive link and tag the MAAP numbers. Ben/Jordan -> will present the pilot plan on Wed 7/29 10am PT if that works for LumaBio.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
